title: lightning might stuck for hours when importing parquet files from cloud storage
body:
## Bug Report

Please answer these questions before submitting your issue. Thanks!

### 1. Minimal reproduce step (Required)

<!-- a step by step guide for reproducing the bug. -->
after https://github.com/pingcap/tidb/pull/46984, including `>= v7.5.x`, `7.1.3+`, we will sample parquet all the time in serial, it's very slow and might takes hours if user have large mount of parquet files before lightning start doing import, and the time takes to sample the files might even longer than real import work.

we only need this size for displaying progress more accurately and use it as a reference when splitting engine, but slowing import this much is un-acceptable.

### 2. What did you expect to see? (Required)
start import fast
### 3. What did you see instead (Required)
it might takes hours before start doing any work
### 4. What is your TiDB version? (Required)

<!-- Paste the output of SELECT tidb_version() -->

comments.author: reporter
comments.body: it's a enhance type of bug, it need to pick back

comments.author: participant1
comments.body: How about sampling just one file? Sample the first file and calculate a compression ratio, and use this compression ratio to estimate the remaining files.

comments.author: reporter
comments.body: lgtm

comments.author: participant2
comments.body:
> How about sampling just one file

@participant1 Do you have real data to support this idea? I'm afraid that different table structure may have different compression ratio, so IMO we should at least sample once for every table. But the performance is not improved if every table only has 1 parquet file.

comments.author: participant1
comments.body: Good catch. The different table structure may have different compression ratio, I will fix #56205 and test with different tables.

comments.author: participant3
comments.body:
I am reopening this issue. The PR #56205 to fix `constructFileInfo` is entirely wrong and does not improve the situation much.

The issue is that ***OPENING A PARQUET FILE IN S3 IS EXTREMELY TIME-COSTLY*** (i.e. `ReadParquetFileRowCountByFile` must be avoided like plague). The PR #56205 changes the original sampling algorithm:

* for each parquet file:
    1. open it ( :-1: )
    2. read the real size
    3. set it as the file's RealSize

to this:

* for each parquet file:
    1. if the table's `sampledParquetRowSizes` is unknown (0),
        1. open it ( :ok: )
        2. read the (real size / count)
        3. store it into the table's `sampledParquetRowSizes`
   2. now that the table's `sampledParquetRowSizes` is known,
        1. open the file again (👎👎👎👎👎👎)
        2. read the count
        3. set (`sampledParquetRowSizes` * count) as the file's RealSize

https://github.com/pingcap/tidb/blob/fc8bdb54c6061fdb0af15c28943d41e5f12d9f0d/pkg/lightning/mydump/loader.go#L540-L566

So you are still reading N files in total before importing. Nothing has changed!

Instead of sampling the ratio as (real size / count), you should use the ratio (real size / file size), because getting the file size is free. Then the other file's RealSize can be calculated just by ((sampled real size / file size) * current file size).

---

I also demand we add a failpoint-enabled integration test, which explodes after opening/downloading files 49 times from `data-source-dir` (i.e. total count of `ReadFile` + `Open`). The test should consist of
* 1 database (`test-schema-create.sql`)
* 4 tables (`test.{a,b,c,d}-schema.sql`)
    * two table with 10 parquet files (`test.{a,b}.[0-9].parquet`)
    * two table with 10 gzip-compressed CSV files (`test.{c,d}.[0-9].csv.gz`)

comments.author: participant3
comments.body:
@reporter You only need an ***upper estimate*** of the row count, you don't need the exact count. Row ID gaps are expected. You could even set `rowCount = realSize`. 

We won't accept solutions that open and read 10000 parquet files before precheck, even with parallelization.

comments.author: reporter
comments.body:
> [@reporter](https://github.com/reporter) You only need an _**upper estimate**_ of the row count, you don't need the exact count. Row ID gaps are expected. You could even set `rowCount = realSize`.

as `realSize` comes from sampling some files, not sure how much it can reflect all files, but it should be fine in most cases

the auto-id range is not always needed, such as when the pk is clustered and data files have provided the auto IDs, maybe we can add auto detect and avoid alloc id range.

> We won't accept solutions that open and read 10000 parquet files before precheck, even with parallelization.

even with sampling, in worst case when table-count ~ O(n) where n is number of files, we still need to read O(n) files

comments.author: participant3
comments.body:
> the auto-id range is not always needed, such as when the pk is clustered and data files have provided the auto IDs, maybe we can add auto detect and avoid alloc id range.

yeah allocating ID at real-time (like TiDB) instead of pre-allocating can also get rid of the estimation, though this would be a quite big refactoring 🙃, and also not so friendly for checkpoints.

> even with sampling, in worst case when table-count ~ O(n) where n is number of files, we still need to read O(n) files

that's true, ideally we should never sampling anything at all. but in practice the number of tables is much less than the number of data files. having (number of files / number of tables >> number of CPU cores) is enough to outperform parallelization.

comments.author: participant4
comments.body:
If opening files with parallelization is still unacceptable, can we estimate a **lower bound** for the parquet compression ratio? Since we can't guarantee that we won't get an underestimated `Rows` using sampling files in some extreme cases.

I did a simple test: I created a extremely simple table, only one column and all values were 1. I used Python PyArrow package to write it as Parquet file. The data page size was set to 1MB and the number of row groups was 1 ([data page](https://tajo.apache.org/docs/0.8.0/table_management/parquet.html) is the basic unit of compression which affects the compression ratio).  Below is the result:

![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/5f9b0a2a-db9d-4d36-a335-9d4f1d0ab09b)

By this way, we can obtain the compression ratio: 20000 / (800m * 8) = 3.125e-06. Then we could use this value to estimate the `Rows` of each file, although we will quite a very large RowID gap 🧐.

> I tested different compression algorithms supported by Parquet. The file size is almost the same so I just take the minimum value.

comments.author: participant4
comments.body:
Or we just skip fetching row count and use the above estimation method only when table has no auto row ID 🥲.
https://github.com/pingcap/tidb/blob/4734c9c2f4a240818bb2d7aac84a4c169318b6e9/pkg/lightning/backend/kv/sql2kv.go#L216-L241

comments.author: participant3
comments.body:
Using 1/320000 as the lower-bound is fine, but that puts an upper limit of the total supported size of Parquet files to (2<sup>64</sup> / 320000) = 52 TiB.

In the long term we should have some way to recover from using rowID outside of the allocated range (the issue is already happening with CSV, see TICKET-5411) and then we can reduce the compression estimation to some more practical value (e.g. 0.7). But that involves refactoring outside the scope of this issue.

> I think we could resolve it like this. Suppose we have 10 chunks:
>
> * chunk 0: rowID in [0, 10)
> * chunk 1: rowID in [10, 25)
> * chunk 2: rowID in [25, 40)
> * ...
> * chunk 9: rowID in [475, 500)
> 
> Suppose we actually *underestimated* the number of rows in chunk 1 and we actually have 50 rows instead of 15 rows. Instead of assigning the row number as [10, 60) which spills into the next chunks, we use
>
> * rows [0, 15) of chunk 1 get ID [10, 25)
> * rows [15, 30) of chunk 1 get ID [510, 525) <- 500 is the max rowID of the entire table
> * rows [30, 45) of chunk 1 get ID [1010, 1025)
> * rows [45, 50) of chunk 1 get ID [1510, 1515)
> 
> This way we can be sure no overlapping will happen, at the same time being checkpoint-friendly as the allocation scheme is stateless. We need to modify the code doing `ALTER TABLE AUTO_INCREMENT` to set it to 1515 instead of 500 though.

BTW does `IMPORT INTO` have the same issue regarding row ID sampling?

comments.author: participant4
comments.body:
> BTW does IMPORT INTO have the same issue regarding row ID sampling?

`IMPORT INTO` will read row number from file because we doesn't set `Rows` in  file meta.

https://github.com/pingcap/tidb/blob/4734c9c2f4a240818bb2d7aac84a4c169318b6e9/pkg/executor/importer/table_import.go#L402

https://github.com/pingcap/tidb/blob/4734c9c2f4a240818bb2d7aac84a4c169318b6e9/pkg/lightning/mydump/region.go#L364-L377

comments.author: reporter
comments.body:
> * rows [15, 30) of chunk 1 get ID [510, 525) <- 500 is the max rowID of the entire table

it's more complex when using parallel import where we use a table to coordinate id allocation, and also considering the range is also saved in checkpoint

reading files in parallel is simpler, if it can finish within a reasonable time, I think it's acceptable for the short term. we can consider optimize id allocation later, including the similar case for CSV
